ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bandit controller for augmentation strength on MS-COCO
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 at 448 pixel resolution on MS-COCO (80 labels) for 60 epochs, using 3 seeds. A contextual bandit with 5 arms picks the augmentation strength at the start of each epoch from three state features: mean loss, tail-label average precision on a held-out split, and the gradient norm ratio of rare to frequent labels. Report mean average precision, tail-label average precision for the 20 rarest labels, overall F1 and epochs needed to reach 95 percent of final precision.
CONTROLS: Baseline: a fixed RandAugment magnitude of 9 with a cosine schedule. Control: the bandit fed shuffled state features. Ablation: dropping the gradient norm feature, and a staged schedule that raises strength at epochs 15 and 45. Differences are tested by paired bootstrap over test images.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: I expect tail-label precision to rise by about 1.5 points and mean average precision by under one point, with convergence somewhat earlier. The controller could fail if state features are too noisy per epoch to separate good from bad strengths.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Policy network for optimizer and criterion choices on MS-COCO
PROPOSAL: Train a ConvNeXt-B at 448 pixel resolution on MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE for 120 epochs, using 5 seeds. At intervals of 2 epochs, a small policy network reads the mean loss, the tail-label average precision and the gradient norm ratio and picks one of 4 optimizer settings and one of 3 criterion choices, trained by a policy-gradient update on validation precision. Report mean average precision, tail-label average precision for the rare labels, overall F1 and epochs needed to reach 95 percent of final precision.
CONTROLS: Baseline: AdamW with a cosine schedule and plain sigmoid loss. Control: the policy network fed shuffled state features. Ablation: restricting it to the loss choice only, and a staged variant that changes settings at epochs 40 and 80, with paired bootstrap on test images.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: I expect tail-label precision to rise by around 1.5 points on both datasets, with fewer epochs to reach the plateau. The policy could fail if rewards are too sparse for consistent gains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Plateau-triggered learning-rate restarts on PASCAL VOC
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 at 224 pixel resolution on PASCAL VOC 2007 (20 labels) for 40 epochs, using 3 seeds. Monitor the validation mean average precision with a window of 3 epochs, and when the gain falls below 0.1 points restart the cosine schedule at 40 percent of the previous peak. Report mean average precision, per-label precision for the 5 rarest labels, and epochs needed to reach 95 percent of final precision.
CONTROLS: Baseline: a single cosine schedule and a staircase schedule with decay at epochs 18 and 32. Control: restarts fired at random epochs, matched in number. Ablation: peak ratios of 20 and 70 percent. Paired bootstrap over test images gives intervals for each gap.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: I expect convergence to be reached about 15 percent sooner and mean average precision to change by under half a point, though the restarts could fail by interrupting good minima and adding oscillation near the end.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient-balance switch between cross-entropy and asymmetric loss on VOC
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 at 224 pixel resolution on PASCAL VOC 2007 (20 labels) for 40 epochs, using 8 seeds. Track the ratio of positive to negative gradient magnitude each epoch, and switch from binary cross-entropy to asymmetric loss with gamma 4 when the ratio drops below 0.2, with three thresholds tried. Report mean average precision, per-label precision for the 5 rarest labels, and epochs needed to reach 95 percent of final precision.
CONTROLS: Baseline: binary cross-entropy alone and asymmetric loss alone, each with 8 seeds. Control: a switch at a fixed epoch matching the mean trigger epoch. Ablation: gamma of 2 and 8, and the ratio measured on batches or epochs. A paired bootstrap over test images gives intervals for each gap.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: I expect the switch to match asymmetric loss on rare labels and beat cross-entropy by under one point on mean average precision. It could fail if the ratio is too noisy to give a stable trigger.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Population-based adaptation of learning rate and loss weights on NUS-WIDE
PROPOSAL: Train a ConvNeXt-T at 384 pixel resolution on NUS-WIDE (81 labels) for 45 epochs, using 4 seeds. Run a population of 8 members, and each 5 epochs copy the weights of the best 2 members to the worst 2, then perturb the learning rate by a bounded factor and the loss weight on rare labels by a bounded step. Report mean average precision, tail-label precision for the 20 rarest labels and overall F1.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the best fixed configuration from a random search of 8 trials with the same training length. Control: perturbation without selection. Ablation: population sizes of 4 and 16 on one seed. A paired bootstrap over test images gives intervals for each gap.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: I expect tail-label precision to rise by about two points over the random search, with mean average precision up by one point, though the method could fail if copying weights shrinks the diversity of the population.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Recurrent scheduler for four training components on NUS-WIDE
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-152 at 448 pixel resolution on NUS-WIDE (81 labels), MS-COCO and PASCAL VOC for 90 epochs, using 3 seeds. At intervals of 3 epochs, a recurrent scheduler emits the augmentation policy, optimizer, step-size factor and objective from the loss history, and is trained by evolution strategies over 24 candidate schedulers. Report mean average precision, tail-label precision for the rare labels and overall F1 on each of 3 datasets.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the best fixed configuration from a random search with 24 trials and matching training length. Control: a scheduler fed a shuffled loss history. Ablation: freezing any one of the 4 components, and schedulers with 2 and 4 candidates fewer, scored with paired bootstrap on test images.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: I expect tail-label precision to rise by about two points over the random search on all datasets. The scheduler could fail if evolution strategies find gains that exist only for the controller seeds used.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tail-aware augmentation gating on PASCAL VOC
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 at 224 pixel resolution on PASCAL VOC 2007 (20 labels) for 30 epochs, using 3 seeds. Images containing a label among the 5 rarest in the training set receive a weaker augmentation, with magnitude 3 against 9 for other images, and the gap closes linearly over training. Report mean average precision, precision for the 5 rarest labels and overall F1, with per-epoch curves saved for later comparison.
CONTROLS: Baseline: uniform RandAugment at a fixed magnitude. Control: weaker augmentation on a random set of images of equal share. Ablation: the closing epoch earlier and later. Paired bootstrap over test images gives intervals for each gap.
COST: 28
PREDICTION: I expect the rarest-label precision to improve by about two points with mean average precision flat. The gating could fail if rare labels co-occur with frequent ones so often that most images count as rare.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint scheduling of four training components on PASCAL VOC
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 at 224 pixel resolution on PASCAL VOC 2007 (20 labels) for 30 epochs, using 3 seeds. At epochs 10 and 20 a threshold-based policy changes the augmentation strength, learning-rate factor, momentum and loss choice according to held-out precision, and the study toggles each of the 4 parts alone and in pairs. Report mean average precision, precision for the 5 rarest labels and overall F1.
CONTROLS: Baseline: a static recipe chosen by grid search of 12 trials. Control: the policy with decisions permuted across epochs. Ablation: the single-part and pairwise toggles named above, each with separate seeds. Paired bootstrap over test images gives intervals for each gap.
COST: 28
PREDICTION: I expect the full scheduler to gain about one point on rare labels, with most of it coming from the loss part and the augmentation part. It could fail if interactions are weak and parts add up with no joint benefit.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sharpness-triggered optimizer switch from AdamW to SGD on MS-COCO
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 at 448 pixel resolution on MS-COCO (80 labels) for 55 epochs, using 2 seeds. Estimate the largest curvature direction with 5 power iterations each epoch, and switch from AdamW to SGD with momentum 0.9 once the estimate plateaus for 3 epochs. Report mean average precision, tail-label precision for the 20 rarest labels, overall F1 and the gap between training and validation loss.
CONTROLS: Baseline: AdamW alone and SGD alone, with cosine schedules. Control: a switch at a fixed epoch equal to the mean trigger epoch. Ablation: plateau windows of 2 and 5 epochs, and 2 power iterations in place of 5. A paired bootstrap over test images gives intervals for each gap.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: I expect the switch to narrow the generalization gap and to lift mean average precision by about half a point over AdamW. It could fail if the curvature estimate is too noisy to give a stable trigger.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive focal exponent driven by label frequency drift on COCO
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 at 448 pixel resolution on MS-COCO (80 labels) for 200 epochs, using 4 seeds. Each epoch, estimate the running positive rate of each label in the batch stream, and assign the focal exponent of that label to a monotone mapping of how far the rate falls below its dataset frequency, with ceiling 4. Report mean average precision, tail-label precision for the 20 rarest labels and overall F1, with checkpoints each 5 epochs.
CONTROLS: Baseline: focal loss with a fixed exponent of 2, and plain sigmoid loss. Control: exponents assigned from shuffled label frequencies. Ablation: ceilings 2 and 8, and updating each 10 epochs in place of each epoch. Intervals come from paired bootstrap.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: I expect tail-label precision to improve by about two points with mean average precision up by half a point. The scheme could fail if early exponent estimates are unstable and destabilize rare-label learning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Label-correlation mixup with a staged curriculum on VOC and COCO
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 at 224 pixel resolution on PASCAL VOC 2007 and a 20-label subset of MS-COCO for 30 epochs, using 3 seeds. Mix pairs of images whose label sets overlap by at least one label, and raise the mixing probability from 0.1 to 0.5 as the validation precision on rare labels stalls. Report mean average precision, precision for the 5 rarest labels and overall F1.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard mixup with probability 0.3 and no mixup. Control: mixing pairs drawn without regard to label overlap. Ablation: overlap thresholds of two labels, and the increase triggered at fixed epochs 10 and 20 in place of the stall rule.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: I expect rare-label precision to rise by about one point on both datasets with mean average precision flat. The approach could fail if mixed images blur the weak signals of rare labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stall-triggered recipe changes on multi-label benchmarks
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 at 224 pixel resolution on PASCAL VOC 2007, MS-COCO, NUS-WIDE, Open Images subsets of 100 labels and a 50-label fashion collection for 30 epochs, using 3 seeds. Augmentation strength and criterion are changed by a threshold-based controller when held-out precision on rare labels stalls for 2 epochs. Report mean average precision, precision for the 5 rarest labels and overall F1 at 5 checkpoints per run on the 5 datasets.
CONTROLS: Baseline: a static recipe with magnitude 9 and binary cross-entropy. Control: the controller fed shuffled validation signals. Ablation: stall windows of 1 and 4 epochs, and an augmentation-only controller. Each comparison uses paired bootstrap over test images on each dataset.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: I expect rare-label precision to rise by about one point on most datasets with mean average precision flat. The controller could fail if stall signals differ between datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cosine restarts triggered by loss plateau in a small multi-label model
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-18 at 224 pixel resolution on PASCAL VOC 2007 (20 labels) for 45 epochs, using 3 seeds. Restart the cosine learning-rate schedule when the training loss gain over 3 epochs falls below 2 percent, with the restart peak at 60 percent of the original. Report mean average precision, precision for the 5 rarest labels and epochs needed to reach 95 percent of final precision.
CONTROLS: Baseline: a single cosine schedule and a staircase schedule with decay at epochs 24 and 32. Control: restarts at random epochs, matched in number. Ablation: peak ratios 30 and 80 percent. Intervals come from paired bootstrap over test images.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: I expect faster convergence by around 10 percent and mean average precision changing by under half a point, though the restarts could fail by disturbing good minima near the end of training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Trust-region learning-rate controller from curvature in a deep backbone
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-152 at 384 pixel resolution on PASCAL VOC 2007 and MS-COCO for 80 epochs, using 3 seeds. Each 100 steps, estimate local curvature with 5 Hessian-vector products and choose the learning rate as a trust-region fraction of the inverse, bounded between 0.1 and 10 times the cosine schedule. Report mean average precision, precision for the rare labels and epochs needed to reach 95 percent of final precision.
CONTROLS: Baseline: cosine and step schedules, tuned with 5 trials each. Control: learning rates drawn at random from the same bounds. Ablation: estimate intervals of 50 and 400 steps, and bounds of 0.3 and 3 times. Intervals come from paired bootstrap over test images.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: I expect faster convergence by around 15 percent and mean average precision within half a point of the baselines. The controller could fail if curvature estimates are too noisy to guide the learning rate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient-conflict weighting between frequent and rare label groups
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 at 384 pixel resolution on NUS-WIDE (81 labels) for 35 epochs, using 3 seeds. Split labels into a frequent half and a rare half, measure the cosine between their gradients each 200 steps, and when it turns negative raise the loss weight of the rare half from 1 to 3. Report mean average precision, precision for the 20 rarest labels and overall F1.
CONTROLS: Baseline: static loss weights of 1 and of 3 on the rare half. Control: the weight raised at random steps, matched in number. Ablation: a split into 4 groups, and measuring the cosine each 100 and 800 steps. Paired bootstrap over test images gives intervals.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: I expect rare-label precision to rise by about 1.5 points and mean average precision by half a point. The scheme could fail if gradient cosines are negative nearly always, leaving the weight at its ceiling.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evolutionary search of training trajectories on a proxy subset of NUS-WIDE
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 at 224 pixel resolution on 20 percent of NUS-WIDE (81 labels) for 30 epochs to evaluate 60 candidate trajectories, each a sequence of augmentation magnitude, learning-rate multiplier and objective for 3 phases, using 3 seeds. Evolve it for 12 rounds, then retrain the best 5 trajectories on the full data. Report mean average precision, precision for the 20 rarest labels and overall F1.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the best of 60 random trajectories under the same protocol, and the static default recipe. Control: the evolved trajectories with phase order reversed. Ablation: populations of 20 and 100, and shorter phases. Intervals come from bootstrap.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: I expect rare-label precision to rise by about 1.5 points and mean average precision by half a point after retraining. The search could fail if rankings on the proxy subset do not carry over to the full set.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Imitation of tuned schedules with a learned scheduler on COCO
PROPOSAL: Train a ConvNeXt-T at 384 pixel resolution on MS-COCO (80 labels) for 60 epochs, using 4 seeds. Log 30 tuned training runs, then fit a gradient-boosted model that maps the state at each epoch (loss, tail-label precision, gradient norm ratio) to the next learning-rate multiplier and augmentation magnitude, and use it online for new runs. Report mean average precision, tail-label precision for the 20 rarest labels and overall F1.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the best of the 30 logged configurations and a cosine schedule. Control: the scheduler fitted on state-shuffled logs. Ablation: fitting on 10 and 20 logged runs, and dropping the gradient feature. Paired bootstrap over test images gives intervals.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: I expect the learned scheduler to match the best logged run on mean average precision and to gain about one point on rare labels. It could fail if the logged runs share too little variety to cover states met online.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hypernetwork scheduler trained on logged runs on MS-COCO
PROPOSAL: Train ResNet-50, ResNet-101, ConvNeXt-T and ConvNeXt-B networks at 384 pixel resolution on MS-COCO (80 labels) for 90 epochs, using 2 seeds. Log 90 tuned runs, then fit a hypernetwork that maps the state at each epoch to the next learning-rate multiplier, augmentation magnitude, optimizer setting and objective, and use it online for new runs. Report mean average precision, tail-label precision for the 20 rarest labels and overall F1 for each backbone.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the best of the 90 logged configurations and a cosine schedule, for each backbone. Control: the hypernetwork fitted on state-shuffled logs. Ablation: fitting on fewer runs, and a variant restricted to 2 outputs. Paired bootstrap over test images gives intervals.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: I expect the learned scheduler to match the best logged run on mean average precision and to gain about one point on rare labels for every backbone. It could fail if logged runs for one backbone transfer poorly to the others.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-gradient adaptation of loss weights on PASCAL VOC
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 at 224 pixel resolution on PASCAL VOC 2007 (20 labels) for 36 epochs, using 3 seeds. Every 100 steps, take one meta-gradient step on per-label loss weights using a clean validation batch of 128 images, with meta learning rate 0.01 and weights clipped to the interval 0.5 to 4. Report mean average precision, precision for the 5 rarest labels, overall F1 and epochs needed to reach 95 percent of final precision.
CONTROLS: Baseline: uniform weights and inverse-frequency weights. Control: meta-gradient steps on a batch with shuffled labels. Ablation: meta learning rates 0.003 and 0.03, and validation batches of 32 and 512. Paired bootstrap over test images gives intervals.
COST: 110
PREDICTION: I expect rare-label precision to rise by about two points with mean average precision up by half a point. The method could fail if weights drift toward the validation batch and lose generality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive per-label weights driven by validation precision on VOC
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 at 224 pixel resolution on PASCAL VOC 2007 (20 labels) for 120 epochs, using 10 seeds. Adapt per-label loss weights by a procedure that raises the weight of any label whose validation precision trails the running mean by a threshold, with thresholds 0.02, 0.05 and 0.1, 3 weight ceilings and 3 learning-rate schedules. Report mean average precision, precision for the 5 rarest labels, overall F1 and epochs needed to reach 95 percent of final precision.
CONTROLS: Baseline: uniform weights and inverse-frequency weights under the 3 schedules. Control: the procedure applied to shuffled validation precision. Ablation: update periods of 1, 5 and 20 epochs. Paired bootstrap over test images gives intervals.
COST: 110
PREDICTION: I expect rare-label precision to rise by about two points with mean average precision up by half a point. The procedure could fail if validation noise drives weights to the ceiling.
